newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher on hectic fund bids.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher on hectic fund bids.

text.p: Delhi shares ended sharply higher in hectic trade on Friday on large bids by domestic and foreign funds, traders said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange benchmark index ended 11.47 points higher at 732.49 points.

Traders said punters covered short positions after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said the government would soon announce its decision on a controversial minimum tax imposed on company profits. The tax was announced in the last federal budget.
Reports that the government was likely to announce a package to boost capital markets in the next fortnight also cheered investors, traders said.
"Revival of buying by foreign funds has brought a sharp change in the market's behaviour," said Vinod Aggarwal at Mass Financial Services.
Shares of two-wheeler maker Bajaj Auto jumped 53.55 rupees to 992. Auto firm Hero Honda gained five rupees to 295.
Hindustan Lever shot up 37.50 rupees to 892.50 and ITC climbed 13.45 rupees to 342.
